titles.to: A Moustache That Has Played Macbeth

replace.find: "Phil, you look drowned," said the parlour maid
replace.with: "Miss Philippa, you look drowned," said the parlour maid

replace.find: Her pug, Bismarck, snored
replace.with: Her pug, Foots, snored

replace.find: Bismarck snorted in his sleep
replace.with: Foots snorted in his sleep

replace.find: Bismarck woke, barked once
replace.with: Foots woke, barked once

replace.find: Bismarck was transferred to her arm
replace.with: Foots was transferred to her arm

replace.find: Three a month for Mr Pye in Fleet Street.
replace.with: Three a month for Mr Beadle in Fleet Street.

replace.find: "Prefer what?" Constance asked quickly. Too quickly.
replace.with: "Prefer what?" Constance asked, a shade too fast.

replace.find: I have buried two husbands and outlived three doctors,
replace.with: I have buried a husband and outlived two doctors,

replace.find: I know guilt the way a cook knows butter. Scoot.”
replace.with: I know guilt the way a cook knows butter. Make room.”

replace.find: Philippa scooted.
replace.with: Philippa made room.

replace.find: "Aunt! Mrs Marlowe! Mr Glennie
replace.with: "Godmama! Mrs Marlowe! Mr Glennie

replace.find: It was not Fipps at all. It was Constance's maid, Ellis, in a borrowed coat and hat,
replace.with: It was not Fipps at all. It was Ellis, the younger of Augustine's housemaids, bribed with a hat ribbon, in a borrowed coat and hat,

replace.find: They lingered half a second too long at the ribbon.
replace.with: They stayed at the ribbon after the spectacles were straight.

replace.find: Rain tapped the drawing room windows in Queen's Gate.
replace.with: Rain tapped the drawing room windows in Campden Hill Square.

replace.find: Philippa came down with ink on her cuff and a letter folded twice.
replace.with: Philippa arrived from her lodgings with ink on her cuff and a letter folded twice.

replace.find: borrowed from the housekeeper's mourning
replace.with: borrowed from her landlady's mourning

replace.find: Foots sneezed in his sleep and paddled his feet.
replace.with: Foots sneezed in his sleep and did not wake.

replace.find: "Grief also makes heiresses inconveniently eligible
replace.with: "Grief also makes young women inconveniently eligible

replace.find: He kept Aunt's matchmaking at bay for two years
replace.with: He kept your matchmaking at bay for two years

replace.find: Only you doing my father's brewery sums in the margins of my dreadfuls.
replace.with: Only you doing your father's brewery sums in the margins of my dreadfuls.

replace.find: "Her ladyship says brandy is medicinal,"
replace.with: "Madam says brandy is medicinal,"

replace.find: "Shall I tell her ladyship Captain Bunting
replace.with: "Shall I tell Madam Captain Bunting

replace.find: "Mr Tibbs, of Tibbs and Hall, Fleet Street," Augustine said.
replace.with: "Mr Tibbs, Mr Beadle's partner in Fleet Street," Augustine said.

replace.find: a lady, six and twenty, with spectacles
replace.with: a lady, seven and twenty, with spectacles

replace.find: then killed him to keep your wedding at bay
replace.with: then killed him to keep my wedding at bay

replace.find: Silence filled the Queen's Gate drawing room.
replace.with: Silence filled the Campden Hill Square drawing room.

replace.find: a woman who can balance Tibbs and Hall can balance anything
replace.with: a woman who can balance Beadle and Tibbs can balance anything

replace.find: "My dear Pippa. You invented a captain
replace.with: "My dear Philippa. You invented a captain

replace.find: "Pippa, your mother was my sister.
replace.with: "Philippa, your mother was my sister.

replace.find: Pippa writes her governesses and stops inventing soldiers.
replace.with: Philippa writes her governesses and stops inventing soldiers.

replace.find: Wedding eve, though there is no wedding. We will drink
replace.with: A week early for a wedding, which is the only punctual way to arrive at one that is not happening. We will drink

notes: Retitled all six (ch1/ch3 shared 'The Double Wedding'; ch4-6 titles were shifted one chapter late). Unified pug (Foots), Augustine's house (Campden Hill Square), publisher (Beadle; Tibbs now his partner), Ellis as Augustine's housemaid, Philippa living in lodgings, age 27, 'Pippa' kept as Constance's name only, one husband/two doctors, 'a week before' vs 'wedding eve'; fixed 'my father's' sums, 'her ladyship', 'Scoot'. Left the heavy smell-per-paragraph texture alone.
